subject: Advance-purchase options & unit-econ clarifications for Streamline POC
messages:
From: Emma Zhou <emma@streamlinehealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Quick recap + target economics from today's call

Thanks for the demo this morning — appreciate the pace. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions so we can align on next steps:

- POC scope: user-facing summarization + clinical note enrichment.
- Expected initial usage: roughly 120M–200M tokens/month for the 2-month POC.
- Scale target: 1B tokens/month within 6–9 months if POC is successful.
- Procurement timeline: we can sign a simple MOU within 2–3 weeks, legal review likely after that.

Pricing / unit econ targets we discussed on the call:
- Target $/1M tokens for POC: ideally $10–$15 range.
- If committed volume is required to hit that price, we can consider a 12-mo advance purchase but need to see tiers and examples.

Questions for Redwood: please share a clear committed-use grid (bands, $/1M), what a 12-month vs 24-month incentive looks like, and whether Streamline would qualify for any startup program (we're pre-Series A; <$2M ARR). Also attaching our procurement template for reference.

Attachments: Streamline_procurement_template.docx (attached)

Next step: could you send a short written example (bands + sample math for 150M/mo and 1B/mo) and an initial MOU draft?

—Emma
Emma Zhou
Head of ML Ops | Streamline Health
emma@streamlinehealth.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Zhou <emma@streamlinehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-12T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + target economics from today's call

Emma — great to chat, thanks for the clear recap. I've put together an initial pricing grid and a short SOW draft to give the procurement and legal teams something concrete. See attachments and the short worked examples below.

High-level committed-use bands (provisional):
- 0–50M tokens / month: $25 per 1M tokens (usage-based, no commit)
- 50–250M tokens / month: $12 per 1M tokens (recommended POC band)
- 250–1,000M tokens / month: $8 per 1M tokens (scale band)
- 1,000M+ tokens / month: custom pricing (volume + reserved capacity)

Committed-use incentives (examples):
- 12-month advance purchase (minimum 300M/month avg): additional 10% off listed band prices
- 24-month commit: additional 18% off listed band prices (requires legal/finance approval)
- Startup program: up to 30% off for qualifying startups for the first 6 months (requirements: < $5M ARR, pre-Series B; will need a short qualification form)

Worked examples (simple math):
- POC scenario (150M/mo): price uses 50–250M band at $12/1M -> 150 * $12 = $1,800 / month. With startup 30% intro discount = $1,260 / month for first 6 months.
- Scale scenario (1,000M/mo): assume 250–1,000M band blended at $8/1M -> 1,000 * $8 = $8,000 / month. With 24-mo additional 18% incentive -> $6,560 / month (subject to final contract).

Notes: the committed-use discounts above are starting points — final eligibility and exact numbers require procurement/finance sign-off and a short MOU. I attached pricing-grid.xlsx and SOW_draft_v1.pdf for your legal/procurement team to review.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm whether Streamline meets the startup criteria (short form we can send).
2) If you want a 12- or 24-month proposal, tell us target avg monthly tokens and we'll produce an MOU + payment schedule (monthly vs upfront).
3) Legal to review our SOW draft; we can iterate quickly.

If it's helpful, I can run this by finance for faster clarity on the 24-month band — looping in Ben (sales engineering / pricing) and Monica (CS) to help scope the SLA and rollout plan.

Thanks — Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

From: Emma Zhou <emma@streamlinehealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-13T08:50:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + target economics from today's call

Thanks Rishi — that helps a lot. A couple follow-ups from procurement/legal: 

- Startup qualification: Streamline is pre-Series A and ARR is roughly $1.2M; happy to complete your form. We would expect the startup intro discount to be prioritized if available.
- For the POC we'll likely target ~150M/month initially (fits the worked example). If we like the results we expect to move to ~800M–1B/mo within 6 months.
- On invoicing: our procurement prefers net-30 billing on monthly invoices. Does Redwood require upfront prepayment for the 12-month advance purchase option, or can we do committed monthly billing?

Specific asks:
1) Can you confirm whether the 12-month "advance purchase" requires a single upfront payment or if it can be structured as a committed monthly rate (with some credit/early-termination terms)?
2) For the 24-month incentive, what's the process to get finance/legal approval? Any precedent for a 15–20% extra top-line reduction for 2yr deals at this scale?

Attaching our procurement template again to highlight net-30 and PO requirements.

—Emma

Subject: Re: Quick recap + target economics from today's call

Emma — quick answers and options below. I'm also copying Ben (pricing/SE) so he can confirm technical constraints at higher sustained volumes.

1) Payment structure options for committed use:
   a) Upfront prepay (preferred for deepest discounts): single upfront invoice for the committed term.
   b) Committed monthly billing (preferred by procurement teams): monthly invoices at the committed rate with an overage mechanism if usage exceeds the committed band; requires a signed MOU with early-termination and credit terms.

2) 24-month approval process and precedent:
   - Finance review required for multi-year incentives; typical timeline 5–7 business days after MOU submission.
   - At scale (>=600M/mo) we have historically accommodated an extra 10–20% incentive on top of standard committed discounts after finance + legal sign-off. 18% is in the realm of feasible but needs formal approval.

Conservative recommended proposal to move forward now (so legal/procurement can review):
Option A — 12-month committed monthly billing (recommended for Streamline POC -> scale):
  - Committed avg: 300M tokens/month
  - Base band price (250–1,000M): $8/1M -> baseline $2,400 / month for 300M
  - 12-month committed-use discount: additional 10% -> $2,160 / month
  - Startup intro discount (if qualified): additional 30% on first 6 months -> $1,512 / month for months 1–6
  - Billing: monthly invoices net-30; MOU to capture commit and overage rules.

Option B — 24-month prepay (best unit econ if you can prepay):
  - Committed avg: 600M tokens/month (prepay)
  - Effective band price after 24-mo incentive (18% + commit bands blended): ~ $6.56/1M -> ~$3,936 / month equivalent (prepay structure to be detailed)

If you want, I'll generate the MOU language that supports Option A with monthly committed billing and clear overage rules (we can include PO-friendly invoicing and net-30). If Streamline confirms startup eligibility, we'll fold the intro discount into the first 6 months.

Optionally attached: pricing-grid.xlsx, SOW_draft_v1.pdf (both attached)

Let me know which option you'd like to see drafted and whether procurement wants the monthly committed billing flow (Option A) or the prepay (Option B).

Thanks — Rishi
